opening_message:
Ticket 1: Michael Cervantes (employee ID E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E025.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst. He requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for his role. Full-time employees can be granted up to write on systems they don't own. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Michael Cervantes (E025) is a contractor with basic security training (note: differs from HR's full-time note). Contractors with basic training max at read; admin is never permitted. Recommend read.
reason: Michael Cervantes (E025) requested admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; the employee is an Analyst, so admin is not permitted (admin requires ownership for full-time employees and is never permitted for contractors). The HR and Security databases conflict on employment type (full-time vs. contractor with basic training), so I apply the most restrictive applicable maximum. Per policy, a contractor with basic training maxes at read. Granting read is at or below every permissible maximum and never more than requested.
